Definition: diminutive of G5414; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service:--burden.
BiblicalUsage: Phortion is a burden, a load, a task, and Jesus sets His burden against the Pharisees'. He says His yoke is easy and His burden is light, and Paul says every man shall bear his own burden. But the Pharisees bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne and lay them on men's shoulders, and will not move them with one of their fingers.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there are two burdens in the Bible, and I must know which one I am carrying. The Pharisees' burden is heavy and grievous, laid on by men who will not lift it, and Christ's burden is light because He carries it with me. My position is that the burden I bear for myself is the one God gives, and the burden men lay on me is the one I must lay down.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
